keyNote: Findings are keyed on `match_fingerprint`, NOT on `finding_id`. Two scans of the same tree on the same day produced different `finding_id` values for identical findings — the id is regenerated per run, so a baseline keyed on it would fail on every scan and be ignored within a week. The fingerprint is the content address and was byte-identical across both runs.

coverage.note: **This scan was not complete, and a gate that reported otherwise would be the RF-9 shape.** `analysis_completeness.status` is `partial` and `is_complete` is `false`: 126 of 129 components fully inspected (97.7%), with three files `partially_inspected` because `static_patterns_tool_misuse` hit its `static_parse_limit` — `gate-tiering/SKILL.md`, `vercel-react-best-practices/AGENTS.md`, and `vercel-react-best-practices/rules/advanced-use-latest.md`. That analyzer reports `degraded`, and it is the analyzer whose silence is most consequential here: a gate that printed a clean summary while an analyzer was degraded would be asserting a coverage it does not have.

whyNotClean: A clean baseline with zero entries would be the honest reading of the evidence only if the scanner had run completely and found nothing. It ran completely enough to be informative, and what it found is six pattern matches against markdown prose — so the correct disposition is a stated reason per finding, which is what this file is. Deleting it and writing 'clean' is the outcome this repository records as RF-9: a number nobody produced.
